scope: Isolated S1 frame group checkpoint. One new probe lists every child frame of a view with its parent frame, pipeline, liveness, crash details, pending state, and event loop. Two new fixture groups, each run for a script-thread unwind in both modes and for content-process exit and kill in multiprocess mode, cover one failure that ends several frames of one view and one failure that ends a frame together with the frame inside it. The patch's notice and containment behavior is unchanged. The parts now have 52, 11, and 32 cases. No product dependency or runtime configuration changes.

configuration.part_check: Each part runs as its own fixture process. Each part must print exactly its own case markers, ending with its summary marker, and the summary must report its own case count. Each repeat must then cover 63 cases in single-process mode or 95 cases in multiprocess mode, each once.
configuration.notice_check: Every contained case captures the parent's frame notices inside the barrier, while the parent's script thread still waits and the frame cannot navigate. It requires exactly one notice that names the parent's identity, exactly the failed frame's browsing context and failed pipeline, and the exact reason. The failed pipeline is the frame's current pipeline, or the pending pipeline for a failed pending or first navigation. After the error page, the late data, and a 300-millisecond settle, the parent still has exactly one notice. The parent-loop popup, the child-site popup, and the independent view have none. In the same-site pending cases, the parent's own document fails, and neither the parent nor the parent-loop popup has a notice.
configuration.send_check: frame-send-failure loads a cross-site child alone in its own event loop. Inside the parent's barrier, the probe closes the constellation's channel to that event loop and sends one GetTitle message through send_message_to_pipeline. The send fails with the channel's own error. No script thread unwinds and no process exits. The frame's crash details and the notice reason must begin with "Send failed (", which only handle_send_error builds.
configuration.history_check: javascript-url-history-crash-recovery loads a start page and a source page, replaces the source entry with a javascript: URL result, and loads a next page, for three entries. The next page's script thread unwinds. The crash page must report two entries. Back must reach the start page, forward must restore the crash page, and back must reach the start page again. The result text and marker never appear, and every earlier identity is stale.
configuration.group_check: frame-siblings-failure and frame-nested-failure, with their process exit and kill variants, load a parent that runs in another event loop than the failed frames. The siblings parent has a healthy same-origin frame in the parent's own event loop, then two frames of one cross-site origin. The nested parent has one cross-site frame that contains a frame of its own origin. Before the failure, the new probe must show every frame live with no crash details and no pending pipeline, the failed frames in the newest frame's event loop, and, for siblings, the healthy frame in another loop. Inside the parent's barrier the notice must have arrived exactly once, naming the parent's identity and exactly the outermost failed frames with their failed pipelines, in any order, with the exact reason. The failed pipelines must be closed, the healthy frame's record must be unchanged, and the parent must have no revocation, crash notification, or terminal callback. After release, all eight callbacks must succeed in the same document. Each outermost failed frame must then have a new live pipeline with crash details that begin with the reason, in an event loop other than the failed one, with distinct pipelines. A nested frame's browsing context must be absent. The parent's view of its frames, its readiness, and its notices must not change after 300 milliseconds. Reload must load every frame again without crash details, and a new URL must recover.

engine_patch.change: One experimental probe: WebView::child_frames_for_document_scope_probe, the EmbedderToConstellationMessage::ChildFramesForDocumentScopeProbe message, its constellation handler, and its tracing target. It lists every child browsing context of the view with its parent browsing context, current pipeline, whether the pipeline is live, its crash details, whether the frame has a pending pipeline, and the Debug text of its pipeline's event loop identifier. Hunk headers were recounted. No notice, containment, recovery, or send-error behavior changed.

fixture_changes: FrameGroup, ChildFrame, child_frames, same_frames, group_notice, and frame_group_failure are new. FrameGroup::Siblings and FrameGroup::Nested select the two layouts.
The intercepted frame-site responses add an inner frame for the nested outer path.

frame-siblings-failure and frame-nested-failure join the frames part. frame-siblings-process-exit, frame-siblings-process-kill, frame-nested-process-exit, and frame-nested-process-kill join the processes part.
The runner case lists, scope text, and runner test counts change to 52, 11, and 32 cases, with 63 shared and 95 multiprocess cases.
findings: The current patch already meets the contract for both layouts. One failure that ends two sibling frames sends exactly one notice that names both frames, and the healthy sibling in the parent's event loop keeps its pipeline.

For a frame and the frame inside it, the notice names only the outer frame, and only the outer frame navigates to an error page. The inner frame's browsing context closes with its parent. Two independent guards enforce this: contained_failed_frames skips a frame whose parent pipeline ran in the failed event loop, and the post-close filter drops a frame whose browsing context or parent pipeline no longer exists. Removing only the first guard passes every case. Removing both makes the notice name the inner frame.
No patch behavior needed to change. The only patch change is the new read-only probe.
A parent reads the nested frame's frame count through the cross-origin window before the failure (1) and after it (0), which shows the error page replaced the outer frame.

The frames part grew from 21.5 to 21.6 seconds to 28.5 to 28.7 seconds in multiprocess mode, and the processes part from 14.7 to 14.8 seconds to 18.0 to 18.3 seconds. The documents part took longer than in the previous checkpoint (37.8 to 38.1 seconds against 35.0 to 35.1) with no change to its cases. This checkpoint keeps all fixture and runner deadlines. negative_controls.variation: The final patch, with the notice loop of handle_event_loop_failure changed to send one notice for each failed frame instead of one notice for each surviving view. Each notice names one frame. The edit replaces the notified-views skip and the per-view frame filter with a filter on the frame's own browsing context. Everything else, including the fixture, is final.

engine_overrides.servo-constellation/constellation.rs: Edited in the preparation's copied sources after the final patch applied. See engine_override_note.

negative_controls.observed_failure: In both modes, the frames part passes the nine earlier cases and fails at frame-siblings-failure with 'Unexpected frame failure notices', listing two notices that each name one of the two sibling frames. The multiprocess processes part passes twenty-five cases and fails at frame-siblings-process-exit with the same message and the reason 'Content process disconnected'. The first single-process frames run printed its error and then exited with signal 11 during teardown, after a SpiderMonkey mutex error. The other runs exited with status 1. The documents part passed in all runs.
negative_controls.interpretation: The single-frame cases cannot distinguish one notice for a view from one notice for each frame. Only a view with several failed frames in one failure depends on the per-view notice.

limitations: Multiprocess evidence uses unsandboxed children on macOS arm64 with software rendering.
The siblings and nested layouts fail through a script-thread unwind, content-process exit, and host SIGKILL. A failed send covers only a single loaded child, and a group has no send fixture.
A frame inside a frame whose own parent is healthy, and a nested failure whose inner frame runs in a different event loop than its failed parent, have no fixture.
The error page's sandboxing flags and opaque origin are shown as before: the parent reads a cross-origin error from it, its crash details begin with the reason, and no probe reads its flags directly.
Process exit and kill of a group in multiprocess mode do not identify the nested inner frame's process, because the probe reports only the newest child frame's process.
The nested inner frame's membership in the failed event loop is shown by its identical event loop identifier before the failure, not by a process id.
The send-error caller, the real dead script thread, and the javascript: URL history gaps from the previous checkpoint remain open.
No new Linux, native-input, release-performance, or remote CI evidence is claimed.
